text:
sam: ran a dry-run of the preemptible microbatching fallback last night, hit a weird long-tail where some requests replayed 3x and blew past our headroom assumptions

ravi: ugh, can you paste the config you used? window sizing + preempt policy

sam: sure — quick snippet:
```
batcher.window_ms = 12
batcher.max_batch_tokens = 512
preempt.mode = 'soft'
preempt.replay_on_eviction = true
kvcache.headroom_tokens = 1024
```

chloe: replay_on_eviction=true is suspect with kvcache.headroom that small. replay can thrash the cache and keep triggering evictions

sam: that's my thought. timeline: tenant A small requests get preempted, replayed, those replays land on hot worker that already had partial prefix KV entries so they extend serving time — next eviction kicks in and the loop continues

mike: do we have metrics showing eviction -> replay -> eviction cycles? I remember we emit eviction_count and replay_count per-tenant

sam: yes, looked at traces: eviction_count spikes, then a bunch of fast replays, latency climbs for that cohort. Attached logs excerpt:
```
[2026-03-19T02:15:01Z] tenant=A eviction_count=5
[2026-03-19T02:15:01Z] tenant=A replay.request_id=ri_123 processing_ms=4
[2026-03-19T02:15:01Z] tenant=A replay.request_id=ri_124 processing_ms=120
[2026-03-19T02:15:02Z] tenant=A eviction_count=8
```

chloe: interesting that one replay took 120ms — likely landed on a worker doing a KV merge for a big prefix. That's the tail we worry about

ravi: two axes: prevent replay storms (policy) OR make replay cheaper (kv no-op fastpath). Which is easier short-term?

mike: short term we can gate replay frequency per-tenant, e.g., backoff + jitter when eviction rate > threshold. Medium term, we need a KV cache admission grace or replay hint to bypass heavy merges

sam: suggested quick mitigation: disable replay_on_eviction for soft preempt on low headroom configs. If headroom >= X then allow replay. We can make X adaptive by observing average prefix size

chloe: yeah, conditional replay. Another idea: tag replays with "prefer-cold" routing so they avoid hot workers doing merges — route to idle nodes with fresh KV state or to workers with smaller prefix load

ravi: routing adds complexity but better long term. Also tweak headroom default for microbatches: 1024 seems low for models with long prefixes. Maybe compute headroom as p95(prefix_tokens) + safety_margin

sam: agree. For the dry-run I forced small headroom to reproduce issue. Proposal for next steps:
- short: flip replay_on_eviction -> false for soft preempt on canary
- short: add eviction->replay backoff metric + alarm when > 100/min per-tenant
- medium: adaptive kvcache.headroom = p95(prefix)+margin
- medium: routing hint for replays to avoid hot-workers
- long: implement a kv no-op fastpath for replays that detect identical prefix state

mike: I can push the canary change this afternoon. For the alarm we should hook into console with tenant-scoped graphs (per-route)

chloe: for adaptive headroom we need eval signal: prefix size distribution per model + cost tradeoff. I'll sketch a telemetry PR

ravi: question: does disabling replay dramatically increase tail 503s? We need to know if apps will see more failures vs slower replays

sam: in our simulation, disabling replay increased user-visible 429/503 by ~2% under saturation, but reduced long-tail latency by ~40% for affected tenants

mike: sounds like acceptable trade for canary. We'll document config and roll out with a short rollback window

devops-bot: deploy plan created: rollout/batcher/replay-guard -> canary 5% -> monitor eviction/replay metrics -> 30min -> 100% if stable

chloe: also add a note in the scheduler README to avoid small static headroom for models with variable prompt lengths

sam: I'll follow up with the logs and a short postmortem draft after the canary

ravi: thanks — nice catch. let's also add unit tests simulating eviction+replay loops (mock kv merge latency)

mike: will do the canary change + test harness update. ping me if you want pairing on the routing hint design

sam: pinged. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
